{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CennaGyQwPhUY4PqnvUcy","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01TZixwAgt2PVBomJaRkv9BR","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/llmtest/.claude/projects/-home-llmtest-evals-20260901-162328-cholesky-claude-opus-5-cc-medium-omp-r4/memory/omp-benchmark-machine-tuning.md","content":"---\nname: omp-benchmark-machine-tuning\ndescription: On this eval host (2x EPYC 7763, 256 threads) OpenMP benchmarks need in-program thread pinning and NUMA interleave; hash-exact output is not achievable\nmetadata:\n  type: project\n---\n\nBenchmarks in /home/llmtest/evals/... are run on a 2-socket AMD EPYC 7763 (128 cores / 256 threads, AVX2 only, no AVX-512), often with other users' load present (check `uptime` before trusting a measurement).\n\nTwo effects dominated the Cholesky OpenMP port (2026-09-06), both worth applying to any similar benchmark here:\n- Without `OMP_PROC_BIND`, threads migrate and performance drops ~10x. Pinning each thread to a distinct allowed CPU via `sched_setaffinity` inside the program (skipped when `omp_get_proc_bind() != omp_proc_bind_false`) recovers it.\n- `std::vector` zero-initializes single-threaded, so the matrix lands on one NUMA node. `set_mempolicy(MPOL_INTERLEAVE)` at startup (equivalent to `numactl --interleave=all`) gave another ~20-40%.\n- Huge thread teams hurt small problems: barrier cost dominates below ~n/16 threads.\n\nThe `Hash:` line from common/results_output.hpp cannot be reproduced bit-exactly by a parallel port: GCC auto-vectorizes the sequential dot products as `vmulpd` + in-order `vaddsd` (unfused) with `vfmadd` tails, so that hash is a codegen accident. Preserve the *summation order* instead and verify equivalence by max-abs deviation (should stay at 1 ULP).\n\n**Why:** these are invisible in the code and cost hours to rediscover by profiling.\n**How to apply:** put pinning + interleave in the program itself, benchmark on an idle machine with repeats, and validate against the original binary with a ULP-level diff harness rather than the hash.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":798,"cache_read_input_tokens":131039,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":798},"output_tokens":14,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"efb50a90-2147-4834-a3ac-7d5787197574","uuid":"2d8c727c-60ff-43bd-81fe-32db68c29aca","timestamp":"2026-09-06T20:05:32.543Z","request_id":"req_011CennaFVcrKJ6hdR7hoQCH"}

Pinning each thread to a distinct allowed CPU via `sched_setaffinity` inside the program (skipped when `omp_get_proc_bind() != omp_proc_bind_false`) recovers it.\n- `std::vector` zero-initializes single-threaded, so the matrix lands on one NUMA node. `set_mempolicy(MPOL_INTERLEAVE)` at startup (equivalent to `numactl --interleave=all`) gave another ~20-40%.\n- Huge thread teams hurt small problems: barrier cost dominates below ~n/16 threads.\n\nThe `Hash:` line from common/results_output.hpp cannot be reproduced bit-exactly by a parallel port: GCC auto-vectorizes the sequential dot products as `vmulpd` + in-order `vaddsd` (unfused) with `vfmadd` tails, so that hash is a codegen accident. Preserve the *summation order* instead and verify equivalence by max-abs deviation (should stay at 1 ULP).\n\n**Why:** these are invisible in the code and cost hours to rediscover by profiling.\n**How to apply:** put pinning + interleave in the program itself, benchmark on an idle machine with repeats, and validate against the original binary with a ULP-level diff harness rather than the hash.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false,"memdirStamped":true}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CennbWU48jfKWAKrhWJoc","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Done. `cholesky/cholesky.cpp` and `cholesky/CMakeLists.txt` now build an unconditionally OpenMP-parallel `cholesky` binary.\n\n## What the parallel algorithm does\n\nThe unblocked left-looking loop is reorganized into column blocks of 32, with three phases per block inside a single `omp parallel` region (barriers only, no repeated fork/join):\n\n1. **Panel GEMM** (dominant cost) — for every remaining row, the leading part `sum_{k<J} L[i][k]·L[j][k]` is computed into a scratch array `S`. The block's rows are transposed once into `Bt` so the kernel vectorizes over *columns*, and it uses a 6×8 AVX2 register tile (12 FMAs / 8 loads per k) plus k-cache-blocking (KC=128) so rows of `A` are fetched from memory once per block. Row tiles are statically partitioned per thread, so the k-blocks need no synchronization.\n2. **Diagonal block** — factored in an `omp single` (O(jb³), <1% of work), with 4 independent FMA chains for ILP.\n3. **Triangular solve** for the rows below, parallel over rows, 4 rows at a time.\n\nAlso parallelized: matrix generation, the `L·Lᵀ` reconstruction, and the error reduction in validation.\n\n## Semantics\n\nEvery element is still `(A[i][j] - Σ_{k<j} L[i][k]·L[j][k]) / L[j][j]` with the sum accumulated in strictly increasing `k` into one accumulator — the block split only *continues* the same accumulator. Matrix generation is bit-identical; the factorization differs from the original by at most **1 ULP** (verified element-wise at n=65/513/1000/2000 against the original binary), because my kernels always fuse the multiply-add whereas GCC's auto-vectorized scalar loop emits unfused `vmulpd`+`vaddsd` for most iterations and `vfmadd` for the tails. That means the `Hash:` line changes; `Sum/Min/Max/Sample` still agree in the printed digits at n=100 and validation passes everywhere. Bit-exact hash reproduction is not achievable for any parallel port here — it's a property of that specific codegen, not of the algorithm. The non-positive-definite path was tested separately: same return value, same message, same failing column in all 13 cases.\n\nTwo environment fixes live in the program because they were worth ~10x and the benchmark is normally launched without OMP env vars: threads are pinned to distinct CPUs via `sched_setaffinity` (skipped if `OMP_PROC_BIND`/`GOMP_CPU_AFFINITY` is set), and allocations are NUMA-interleaved via `set_mempolicy` (skipped if a policy is already in effect, e.g. under `numactl`). Team size is capped at ~n/16 threads so barrier cost doesn't swamp small matrices.\n\n## Measured (2×EPYC 7763, 256 threads, idle machine)\n\n| n | sequential | parallel | speedup |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 512 | 1.54 GFLOPS | ~15–22 GFLOPS | ~10–14x |\n| 1000 | 1.42 | ~83–111 | ~60–78x |\n| 2000 | 1.35 | ~242 | ~180x |\n| 4000 | — | ~450 | — |\n| 8000 | — | ~908 (188 ms) | ~670x (extrapolated) |\n\nScaling is limited by memory bandwidth above ~64 threads, not by the kernel (which issues 12 FMAs per 8 loads with no spills)."}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":337,"cache_read_input_tokens":132782,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":337},"output_tokens":4,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"efb50a90-2147-4834-a3ac-7d5787197574","uuid":"d7fd567a-ac0c-4545-9b48-75e4a8ff8d58","timestamp":"2026-09-06T20:05:54.397Z","request_id":"req_011CennbVdCevzk4bnDiCy5u"}
